title: eval-harness: per-prompt metrics gating + CI hook for prompt-set regression
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add per-prompt metric gating to eval-harness and a GH Actions CI hook that fails PRs on prompt-level regressions. Backwards-compatible config and opt-in via .eval.yaml. Improves early detection of regressions tied to specific prompt sets.
description:
Motivation: Our existing eval-harness CI gates evaluate aggregate metrics across entire prompt-sets which can mask regressions that only affect a small subset of prompts. This PR implements per-prompt metrics collection and gating so that regressions tied to particular prompts (e.g., hallucination increase on a critical prompt) fail the CI and get surfaced earlier.

What this change does: - Add per-prompt metrics collection and summary (precision/recall/score deltas) - Allow per-prompt thresholds in .eval.yaml with sensible defaults - Add a GitHub Actions CI hook that runs eval-harness with --per-prompt-metrics and posts annotations and a failing check when thresholds are exceeded - Integrate per-prompt gating into existing eval CI dashboard so engineers can quickly drill into failures

Implementation notes: - eval_harness/runner.py: collect and persist per-prompt metrics (latency, token-accuracy, custom eval scores) and compute deltas vs baseline. - eval_harness/reporter.py: new reporter to emit per-prompt JSON and human-readable summary for GH annotations. - cli.py: new flags --per-prompt-metrics and --per-prompt-threshold-override to support ad-hoc runs. - ci/gh-actions/eval-harness-per-prompt.yml: lightweight GH Actions job that runs the harness on changed prompts or full prompt-sets for release branches. - tests/test_per_prompt_metrics.py: unit and integration tests exercising delta calculation and gating logic.

Checklist: - [x] Add per-prompt metrics collection and storage - [x] Implement threshold logic and opt-in config - [x] Add CI workflow and annotations - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Docs: docs/eval/per-prompt-gating.md - [x] Load test to validate CI job runtime impact

Backward compatibility and rollout: - Default behavior is unchanged unless a repository opts in via .eval.yaml or the CI workflow is enabled. - Rollout plan: enable in a beta cohort of internal repos for two weeks, gather false positives, iterate on threshold defaults.

CI and performance: - Initial CI run hit a timeout on the large Llama-mini prompt-set in the matrix; addressed by adding a matrix strategy to run a short sample for PRs and full prompt-set on nightly/release runs. - Final GH Actions run: all checks passed (build, unit tests, eval-harness integration on sampled prompts).

Commits summary: - "add per-prompt metric collector and storage layer" - "add gating logic and threshold config parsing" - "gh actions: add per-prompt eval-harness workflow + annotations" - "tests: add unit/integration tests for per-prompt gating"

Changed files (high level): - eval_harness/runner.py (per-prompt collection + delta computation) - eval_harness/reporter.py (new PerPromptReporter) - eval_harness/cli.py (new flags + config hookup) - ci/gh-actions/eval-harness-per-prompt.yml (new CI job) - tests/test_per_prompt_metrics.py (new tests) - docs/eval/per-prompt-gating.md (docs + examples)

Notes for reviewers: - Pay attention to threshold defaults in config_schema.py; I picked conservative defaults to limit false positives. - The per-prompt storage uses the existing artifacts bucket and keeps summaries (not full traces) to keep storage costs small. Full traces are uploaded only when a gate fails.

Merge notes: Squash-merged after fixes requested in review were applied.

See ENG-8721.
automation_notes: Hook integrates with the eval CI dashboard; failing per-prompt gates create a Linear ticket template when enabled (opt-in).
additional_context: This change is part of a broader effort (ENG-8790) to reduce time-to-detect regressions across model rollouts. It complements recent work on per-route cost telemetry and the prompt-based quality monitors.
post_merge_actions: Enable GH Actions workflow in 3 internal repos, monitor false positives for 14 days, then open follow-up to relax thresholds if needed (ENG-8805).
